source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Record time, date, duration, and frequency of emissions.
3. Use certified monitoring equipment.
4. Measure pollutant levels against regulatory standards.
5. Note weather conditions during the emissions (wind speed, temperature, humidity).
6. Document any visual disturbances or other signs of excessive emissions (smoke plumes, odors, etc.).
7. Identify the source of the emissions.
8. Take photographic or video evidence if possible.
9. Record the type of pollutants detected (e.g., SO2, NOx, VOCs, particulates).
10. Check compliance with industrial permits and regulations.
11. Note any observed operational issues that may contribute to excessive emissions.
12. Compile data from continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS), if available.
13. Compare actual emissions to the facility's emission limits.
14. Document any community complaints or health impacts.
15. List actions taken by the company to address excessive emissions (maintenance, process adjustments).
